newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ruling on EMU accounting to only affect Italy.
newsitem.headline: EU ruling on EMU accounting to only affect Italy.

text.p: A review of European Union budget accounting practices on Friday will only substantively affect Italy's chances of meeting the conditions of a single currency, a senior EU official said.
"No other countries will be affected," said the official when asked whether accounting decisions by Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, will have broader implications.

The review is expected to focus on three areas -- Italy's controversial euro tax, a one-off measure designed to raise 5.5 trillion lire, government financing of state railways (another item which concerns Italy), and the financing of public infrastructure.
The latter may have implications for Germany, the official added, but noted that it would unlikely lead to a change in Germany's proposed budget figures.
For Italy, the euro tax is equivalent to 0.3 percent of gross domestic product, while its financing of state railways amounts to just under 0.2 percent of output, analysts said.
Expectations are that both measures will be approved by Eurostat, leaving Italy's deficit-to-GDP target for 1997 at 3.0 percent, the Maastricht requirement. REUTER
